_note: Single source of truth for the GoStudio template library — image and video. Never hardcode template names, counts, or availability elsewhere — reference this file. If any other file disagrees, this file wins. Update as templates go live.
_usage: Before writing copy that names or counts templates, pull from here. Only status='live' templates may appear in live copy. Templates are a lead product surface under the current positioning (see Pillar 2 in the product marketing context), so this file is expected to grow often.
_maintenance: Created 2026-08-19, intentionally near-empty. The historical '200+ workflows' figure predates this file and was never verified against it — derive counts from this file, do not restate that number. Populate as the template library ships.

columns.name: Customer-facing template name (2-3 words, evocative — see naming convention below)
columns.description: One line saying what you GET, not how it works
columns.creator: Community creator credited, if any (see the creator revenue-share pillar)
columns.slug: URL slug if the template has a landing page (flat L1)

naming_convention._source: Derived from the Creatify.ai gallery teardown — see work-log/marketing-studio/
naming_convention.name: 2-3 word evocative name. Examples of the pattern: 'Crush Test', 'Mystery Box', 'Secret Hack Reveal'.
naming_convention.description: One line starting with an adjective or verb, describing the output the user receives. Example: 'Satisfying crush and durability tests.'
naming_convention.presentation: Three example thumbnails per template card, not one — signals a repeatable format with output variety rather than a single fixed result.

taxonomy_note._warning: Keep these axes separate. Merging them is what produced the duplicate entries observed in the Creatify teardown (Virtual Try-On appeared four times across their tabs).
taxonomy_note.format: What the output looks like — the visual treatment. Suits in-product template naming.
taxonomy_note.job: What the video/image is for — the persuasion job or narrative arc (problem-and-solution, before-and-after, teaser-launch). Suits in-product grouping and is the more durable axis, since formats churn with platform trends.
taxonomy_note.audience_vertical_platform: Who it is for and where it runs. This is the axis for SEO LANDING PAGES, not for template names.
